Accessing curatedMetagenomicData releases with cmgdr

Sean Davis

Source: vignettes/cmgdr.qmd

Background

curatedMetagenomicData (cMD) is a collection of human shotgun metagenomes from published studies, every sample processed through the same pipeline and paired with curated sample metadata, so that profiles from different studies can be compared and pooled. Each sample’s raw reads are quality-controlled and profiled with MetaPhlAn (taxonomic relative abundance), Kraken2/Bracken, a resistome screen against CARD and, in some pipeline configurations, HUMAnN (functional profiles).

The profiles are now published as open data releases at https://cmgd-public.cancerdatasci.org. The layout has a few concepts that the rest of this vignette relies on:

  • A dataset is one pipeline registration: a pipeline version together with its configuration, named <workflow_id>-<version>, for example cmgd_mpa4.2-2.3.0 (pipeline 2.3.0, MetaPhlAn 4.2, no HUMAnN). Profiles from different datasets were made with different tools or databases and are kept apart.
  • A release is an immutable, full snapshot of a dataset, named by its UTC build date (2026-10-16). A release never changes once published; new data arrive as a new release. Cite the dataset and the release id.
  • Each release has a manifest (manifest.json) listing its tables (long, tidy tables such as taxonomic_profile_metaphlan or qc_metrics, stored as Parquet files), ready-made per-study files, and a read-only DuckLake catalog that lets DuckDB query the whole release in place.
  • Every file is listed with its size and SHA-256 checksum. cmgdr downloads files into a local cache and verifies them against those checksums; a file that does not verify is deleted and an error raised. Because releases are immutable, a cached file never goes stale.

The site cannot be listed like a directory: everything is found through JSON indexes, which is what cmgdr reads.

cmgdr is deliberately a low-level client. It knows the published layout and returns plain data frames, lists, local file paths, a DuckDB connection, and (for convenience) a species TreeSummarizedExperiment. It does not reshape, join or model the data; higher-level packages are expected to build on it.

This vignette uses the small cmgd_mpa4.2-2.3.0 release (125 samples in 8 studies) and, within it, the three-sample ZellerG_2014 study, so it downloads only a few hundred kilobytes. All code runs against the live site.

Setup

cmgdr is not on Bioconductor yet. Install it from GitHub; once it is accepted, BiocManager::install("cmgdr") will work.

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("seandavi/cmgdr")

Downloads go to cmgd_cache_dir(), which is tools::R_user_dir("cmgdr", "cache") and moves with the R_USER_CACHE_DIR environment variable. This vignette points it at a temporary directory so building it leaves nothing behind.

library(cmgdr)
Sys.setenv(R_USER_CACHE_DIR = tempfile("cmgdr-cache"))
cmgd_cache_dir()
#> [1] "/tmp/RtmpyhZhDw/cmgdr-cache1bbe1e81e6a7/R/cmgdr"

Finding datasets and releases

cmgd_datasets() takes no required arguments (only base, the site URL) and returns a data frame with one row per published dataset: its id (dataset), the pipeline registration it comes from (workflow_id, version), and the id of its newest release (latest).

datasets <- cmgd_datasets()
datasets
#>               dataset   workflow_id version     latest
#> 1   cmgd_mpa4.2-2.3.0   cmgd_mpa4.2   2.3.0 2026-10-16
#> 2 cmgd_nextflow-2.2.1 cmgd_nextflow   2.2.1 2026-10-08

cmgd_releases() takes a dataset id and returns one row per release of that dataset, oldest first: the release id, its build date, when it was published, and whether it is pinned (kept as a long-term reference).

cmgd_releases("cmgd_mpa4.2-2.3.0")
#>      release release_date                     published_at pinned
#> 1 2026-10-16   2026-10-16 2026-10-16T03:40:40.277445+00:00  FALSE

cmgd_release() opens a release. It takes a dataset id and a release id; the default release = "latest" resolves to the newest one, but for reproducible work pin the id, as here. It reads the release’s manifest and returns a cmgd_release object, the handle every other cmgdr function takes. It is a list with the dataset and release ids, the release URL and the parsed manifest; printing it shows the tables it holds.

rel <- cmgd_release("cmgd_mpa4.2-2.3.0", release = "2026-10-16")
rel
#> <cmgd_release> cmgd_mpa4.2-2.3.0 2026-10-16
#>   url:    https://cmgd-public.cancerdatasci.org/cmgd_mpa4.2-2.3.0/2026-10-16
#>   tables: marker_abundance, marker_presence, metadata_comparison, metadata_sources, qc_metrics, resistome, sample_metadata_cmd, sample_metadata_harmonized, sample_metadata_olm, samples, taxonomic_profile_bracken, taxonomic_profile_metaphlan
class(rel)
#> [1] "cmgd_release"
names(rel$manifest)
#>  [1] "spec_version"          "dataset"               "release"              
#>  [4] "release_date"          "status"                "published_at"         
#>  [7] "run_id"                "source_asset_versions" "artifacts"            
#> [10] "tables"                "provenance"            "lineage"

Tables and files

cmgd_tables() takes a release and returns one row per table: its name, a description, its grain (what one row of the table means), its row_count, and its license. Most tables are CC0-1.0; tables that include values derived from the Olm lab Microbiome Repo are CC-BY-4.0 (see Sample metadata).

tables <- cmgd_tables(rel)
tables[, c("name", "grain", "row_count", "license")]
#>                           name
#> 1             marker_abundance
#> 2              marker_presence
#> 3          metadata_comparison
#> 4             metadata_sources
#> 5                   qc_metrics
#> 6                    resistome
#> 7          sample_metadata_cmd
#> 8   sample_metadata_harmonized
#> 9          sample_metadata_olm
#> 10                     samples
#> 11   taxonomic_profile_bracken
#> 12 taxonomic_profile_metaphlan
#>                                                   grain row_count   license
#> 1                 one row per sample, branch and marker   5013703   CC0-1.0
#> 2         one row per sample, branch and present marker   4688706   CC0-1.0
#> 3           one row per study, field and olm_rows scope        84 CC-BY-4.0
#> 4                            one row per source release         2   CC0-1.0
#> 5                                    one row per sample       125   CC0-1.0
#> 6          one row per sample, branch and CARD template     15582   CC0-1.0
#> 7       one row per sample, field and cMD sample record      2331   CC0-1.0
#> 8                          one row per sample and field       562 CC-BY-4.0
#> 9              one row per sample, field and Olm sample       987 CC-BY-4.0
#> 10                                   one row per sample       125   CC0-1.0
#> 11                 one row per sample, branch and taxon   1223560   CC0-1.0
#> 12 one row per sample, branch, MetaPhlAn pass and clade    127012   CC0-1.0

A table is stored as one or more Parquet files. cmgd_files() takes a release and, optionally, table names, and returns one row per file: the table, the file’s path relative to the release, its full url, its size in bytes, its sha256, and the number of rows it holds.

files <- cmgd_files(rel, "qc_metrics")
str(files)
#> 'data.frame':    1 obs. of  6 variables:
#>  $ table : chr "qc_metrics"
#>  $ path  : chr "tables/qc_metrics/data/part-00000.parquet"
#>  $ url   : chr "https://cmgd-public.cancerdatasci.org/cmgd_mpa4.2-2.3.0/2026-10-16/tables/qc_metrics/data/part-00000.parquet"
#>  $ size  : int 16845
#>  $ sha256: chr "0403bd0b02b62e60d850e007bf81fcab7bf65e193e68faaf8425f3cb17ef216b"
#>  $ rows  : int 125

cmgd_download() takes a release and one path (as in the path column) or full URL, downloads the file into the cache, verifies its size and SHA-256, and returns the local file path. Calling it again returns the cached copy without downloading, as long as the copy still verifies.

local <- cmgd_download(rel, files$path[1])
local
#> [1] "/tmp/RtmpyhZhDw/cmgdr-cache1bbe1e81e6a7/R/cmgdr/cmgd-public.cancerdatasci.org/cmgd_mpa4.2-2.3.0/2026-10-16/tables/qc_metrics/data/part-00000.parquet"
file.size(local) == files$size[1]
#> [1] TRUE

Studies

Besides whole tables, each release has ready-made files for each study. cmgd_studies() takes a release and returns one row per study: its study_name and n_samples.

studies <- cmgd_studies(rel)
studies
#>       study_name n_samples
#> 1  AsnicarF_2017        24
#> 2      BaiX_2021        24
#> 3   DavidLA_2015         1
#> 4       HMP_2012         4
#> 5 LassalleF_2017        23
#> 6  WibowoMC_2021        22
#> 7   ZellerG_2014         3
#> 8    ZhangM_2023        24

cmgd_study_files() takes a release and a study name and returns one row per file published for that study: its name, path, url, size, sha256 and a description of what it holds. There is a species × samples matrix (metaphlan_species.tsv.gz), the study’s rows of the main tables as Parquet, and a QC table (qc.tsv).

study_files <- cmgd_study_files(rel, "ZellerG_2014")
study_files[, c("name", "size")]
#>                       name   size
#> 1          bracken.parquet 253158
#> 2         metadata.parquet   2053
#> 3        metaphlan.parquet  79353
#> 4 metaphlan_species.tsv.gz  14183
#> 5                   qc.tsv   1206
#> 6        resistome.parquet  10860

cmgd_read_study() takes a release, a study and the file’s name without extension ("qc", "metaphlan", "bracken", "metaphlan_species", …), downloads it through the verified cache and reads it into a data frame. Parquet files are read with the duckdb package. The QC table has one row per sample: its keys (sample_key, readset_id, run_ids), read and base counts before and after decontamination, and the pipeline version and commit that produced it.

qc <- cmgd_read_study(rel, "ZellerG_2014", "qc")
str(qc)
#> 'data.frame':    3 obs. of  18 variables:
#>  $ sample_key              : chr  "RS.8G5cd1ZeZW4RVHDQitQ1t5PV7IHCue2p" "RS.bZz5VlfYIkTVYKmDibnmPtWb6pkLWBP9" "RS.l29A5uBFtCKLgc-EPvUhj0hD6Q02Z7qj"
#>  $ sample_id               : chr  "06e398e0194de8d2aa185b9d8996a474" "72080b9ed6d4c860afb54bd9feee501a" "a08d985474ca4b67bb6fc3bb4093e640"
#>  $ readset_id              : chr  "RS.8G5cd1ZeZW4RVHDQitQ1t5PV7IHCue2p" "RS.bZz5VlfYIkTVYKmDibnmPtWb6pkLWBP9" "RS.l29A5uBFtCKLgc-EPvUhj0hD6Q02Z7qj"
#>  $ study_name              : chr  "ZellerG_2014" "ZellerG_2014" "ZellerG_2014"
#>  $ run_ids                 : chr  "ERR478962;ERR478963;ERR480458;ERR480459" "ERR478964;ERR478965;ERR478966;ERR478967;ERR480460;ERR480461;ERR480462;ERR480463" "ERR478958;ERR478959;ERR478960;ERR478961;ERR480454;ERR480455;ERR480456;ERR480457"
#>  $ workflow_id             : chr  "cmgd_mpa4.2" "cmgd_mpa4.2" "cmgd_mpa4.2"

A species TreeSummarizedExperiment

cmgd_species_tse() takes a release and a study and builds a TreeSummarizedExperiment (needs the TreeSummarizedExperiment and Matrix packages) from the study’s species matrix. Rows are MetaPhlAn species clades (full k__...|s__... names), columns are samples (sample_key), and the one assay, relative_abundance, is a sparse matrix of percentages from the main MetaPhlAn pass on all reads. The QC table above is its colData.

tse <- cmgd_species_tse(rel, "ZellerG_2014")
#> Warning: replacing previous import 'S4Arrays::makeNindexFromArrayViewport' by
#> 'DelayedArray::makeNindexFromArrayViewport' when loading 'SummarizedExperiment'
tse
#> class: TreeSummarizedExperiment 
#> dim: 643 3 
#> metadata(0):
#> assays(1): relative_abundance
#> rownames(643):
#>   k__Archaea|p__Methanobacteriota|c__Methanobacteria|o__Methanobacteriales|f__Methanobacteriaceae|g__Methanobrevibacter|s__Methanobrevibacter_smithii
#>   k__Archaea|p__Thermoplasmatota|c__Thermoplasmata|o__Methanomassiliicoccales|f__Methanomassiliicoccaceae|g__Methanomassiliicoccaceae_unclassified|s__Methanomassiliicoccaceae_unclassified_SGB380
#>   ...
#>   k__Eukaryota|p__Ascomycota|c__Saccharomycetes|o__Saccharomycetales|f__Saccharomycetaceae|g__Saccharomyces|s__Saccharomyces_cerevisiae
#>   k__Eukaryota|p__Eukaryota_unclassified|c__Bigyra|o__Opalinata|f__Blastocystidae|g__Blastocystis|s__Blastocystis_sp_subtype_6
#> rowData names(0):
#> colnames(3): RS.8G5cd1ZeZW4RVHDQitQ1t5PV7IHCue2p
#>   RS.bZz5VlfYIkTVYKmDibnmPtWb6pkLWBP9

abundance <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(tse, "relative_abundance")
class(abundance)
#> [1] "dgCMatrix"
#> attr(,"package")

# Shorten the clade names to the species for display
rownames(abundance) <- sub(".*\\|s__", "", rownames(abundance))
top <- order(-Matrix::rowSums(abundance))[1:5]
as.matrix(abundance[top, ])

Sample metadata

Releases since cmgd_mpa4.2-2.3.0 / 2026-10-16 publish sample metadata as tables. cmgd_sample_metadata() takes a release, a source, optional study names and wide, and returns a data frame. The sources are:

  • harmonized (the default): one value per sample and harmonized field, taken from the cMD curation where it has one and from the Olm lab Microbiome Repo otherwise. CC-BY-4.0.
  • cmd: the curatedMetagenomicData curation as published. CC0-1.0.
  • olm: the Olm lab Microbiome Repo, with its route and confidence. CC-BY-4.0.

With wide = FALSE (the default) the table comes back long, as published: one row per sample and field, with the value, the source it came from, the source’s release, and for Olm values the route and confidence.

meta <- cmgd_sample_metadata(rel, study = "ZellerG_2014")
#> sample_metadata_harmonized is licensed CC-BY-4.0; attribution required: cite doi:10.5281/zenodo.23087712
head(meta)
#>     study_name                          sample_key            field
#> 1 ZellerG_2014 RS.8G5cd1ZeZW4RVHDQitQ1t5PV7IHCue2p        age_years
#> 2 ZellerG_2014 RS.8G5cd1ZeZW4RVHDQitQ1t5PV7IHCue2p              bmi
#> 3 ZellerG_2014 RS.8G5cd1ZeZW4RVHDQitQ1t5PV7IHCue2p          country
#> 4 ZellerG_2014 RS.8G5cd1ZeZW4RVHDQitQ1t5PV7IHCue2p health_condition
#> 5 ZellerG_2014 RS.8G5cd1ZeZW4RVHDQitQ1t5PV7IHCue2p              sex
#> 6 ZellerG_2014 RS.bZz5VlfYIkTVYKmDibnmPtWb6pkLWBP9        age_years
#>             value source                                  release   route
#> 1            53.0    cmd 6828fb9abdfc27a91b02e20568d27332eaf19ca4 curated
#> 2            32.0    cmd 6828fb9abdfc27a91b02e20568d27332eaf19ca4 curated
#> 3              FR    cmd 6828fb9abdfc27a91b02e20568d27332eaf19ca4 curated
#> 4 healthy_control    cmd 6828fb9abdfc27a91b02e20568d27332eaf19ca4 curated
#> 5            male    cmd 6828fb9abdfc27a91b02e20568d27332eaf19ca4 curated
#> 6            35.0    cmd 6828fb9abdfc27a91b02e20568d27332eaf19ca4 curated
#>   confidence
#> 1         NA
#> 2         NA
#> 3         NA
#> 4         NA
#> 5         NA
#> 6         NA

Reading a CC-BY-4.0 table prints a message naming the licence and the DOI to cite. The licence and the pinned source releases the table was built from (with their DOIs and checksums) are also attached as attributes, so they travel with the data:

attr(meta, "license")
#> [1] "CC-BY-4.0"
attr(meta, "sources")[, c("source", "release", "doi", "license")]
#>   source                                  release                     doi
#> 1    cmd 6828fb9abdfc27a91b02e20568d27332eaf19ca4                    <NA>
#> 2    olm                                 R2026.25 10.5281/zenodo.23087712
#>     license
#> 1   CC0-1.0
#> 2 CC-BY-4.0

If you use the harmonized or olm tables, cite the Microbiome Repo DOI above as well as curatedMetagenomicData; the provenance lists the full citation text.

With wide = TRUE the result has one row per sample: the sample’s study_name, sample_key, biosample, bioproject and run_accessions, then one character column per field, NA where a sample has no value.

wide <- cmgd_sample_metadata(rel, source = "cmd", study = "ZellerG_2014",
                             wide = TRUE)
dim(wide)
#> [1]  3 25
wide[, c("sample_key", "biosample", "age_years", "sex", "health_condition")]
#>                            sample_key    biosample age_years    sex
#> 1 RS.8G5cd1ZeZW4RVHDQitQ1t5PV7IHCue2p SAMEA2466896   53;53.0   male
#> 2 RS.bZz5VlfYIkTVYKmDibnmPtWb6pkLWBP9 SAMEA2466965   35.0;35   male
#> 3 RS.l29A5uBFtCKLgc-EPvUhj0hD6Q02Z7qj SAMEA2467039   72;72.0 female
#>   health_condition
#> 1  healthy_control
#> 2  healthy_control
#> 3  healthy_control

A release without metadata tables raises an error of class cmgdr_no_metadata, which callers can catch with tryCatch().

Finding samples by run accession

cmgd_find_runs() takes a release and a vector of SRA/ENA run accessions (SRR..., ERR..., DRR...) and looks them up in the release’s samples table, where a sample’s runs are ;-joined. It returns a data frame with one row per accession, in the order given: the run, then the matching samples row (study, sample_key, BioSample, BioProject, pipeline version, …). A run the release does not have gets a row of NAs, so the result always lines up with the input.

runs <- cmgd_find_runs(rel, c("ERR478962", "SRR0000000"))
runs[, c("run", "study_name", "sample_key", "biosample", "bioproject")]
#>          run   study_name                          sample_key    biosample
#> 1  ERR478962 ZellerG_2014 RS.8G5cd1ZeZW4RVHDQitQ1t5PV7IHCue2p SAMEA2466896
#> 2 SRR0000000         <NA>                                <NA>         <NA>
#>   bioproject
#> 1  PRJEB6070
#> 2       <NA>

Provenance

cmgd_provenance() takes a release and returns its provenance.json as a list: the lake snapshots the release was built from (source_asset_versions) and, for releases since 2026-10-16, a cmgd section with the pipeline registration (repository, revision, parameters), the pipeline runs, the reference database versions, the pinned metadata sources, the licence of every table, and citation text.

prov <- cmgd_provenance(rel)
names(prov$cmgd)
#> [1] "registration"     "pipeline_runs"    "databases"        "metadata_sources"
#> [5] "licenses"         "citation"
str(prov$cmgd$databases)
#> List of 4
#>  $ metaphlan      : chr "4.2.6"
#>  $ metaphlan_index: chr "mpa_vJan26_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202605"
#>  $ kraken2_bracken: chr "k2_pluspf_16_GB_20260226"
#>  $ card           : chr "broadstreet-v4.0.1"
prov$cmgd$pipeline_runs
#>   pipeline_version                               git_commit n_samples n_studies
#> 1            2.3.0 793996bafae99c65ce4f9ff85a08f08b68fa6227       125         8
prov$cmgd$citation
#> $cmgd
#> [1] "Pasolli E, Schiffer L, Manghi P, Renson A, Obenchain V, Truong DT, Beghini F, Malik F, Ramos M, Dowd JB, Huttenhower C, Morgan M, Segata N, Waldron L. Accessible, curated metagenomic data through ExperimentHub. Nat Methods. 2017;14(11):1023-1024. doi:10.1038/nmeth.4468"
#> 
#> $olm
#> [1] "Microbiome Repo, OlmLab, release R2026.25 (data package 1.20.0), doi:10.5281/zenodo.23087712; values derived. Required attribution for the CC-BY-4.0 tables."

Whole tables with SQL and dplyr

cmgd_connect() takes a release and returns a DBI connection to an in-memory DuckDB database with the release’s DuckLake catalog attached read-only (needs the DBI and duckdb packages). Every table in cmgd_tables() is available by name. Nothing is downloaded up front: DuckDB fetches only the parts of the remote Parquet files a query needs.

con <- cmgd_connect(rel)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpyhZhDw/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT study_name, count(*) AS n_samples,
         avg(reads_decontaminated) AS mean_reads
  FROM qc_metrics
  GROUP BY study_name
  ORDER BY n_samples DESC")
#>       study_name n_samples mean_reads
#> 1  AsnicarF_2017        24   18436539
#> 2    ZhangM_2023        24   41242176
#> 3      BaiX_2021        24   81421066
#> 4 LassalleF_2017        23   29695992
#> 5  WibowoMC_2021        22   63099853
#> 6       HMP_2012         4   42665646
#> 7   ZellerG_2014         3   70274450
#> 8   DavidLA_2015         1     500546

The same connection works with dplyr (and dbplyr). Here are the five most abundant species in ZellerG_2014, averaged over its samples. A species missing from a sample has no row, so divide by the study’s sample count rather than taking a mean.

library(dplyr)
n <- tbl(con, "qc_metrics") |>
    filter(study_name == "ZellerG_2014") |>
    count() |>
    pull(n)
tbl(con, "taxonomic_profile_metaphlan") |>
    filter(study_name == "ZellerG_2014", rank == "species",
           data_type == "full_data", is.na(humann_bundle)) |>
    group_by(clade_name) |>
    summarise(mean_percent = sum(relative_abundance, na.rm = TRUE) / n) |>
    arrange(desc(mean_percent)) |>
    head(5) |>
    collect() |>
    mutate(species = sub(".*\\|s__", "", clade_name), .keep = "unused")
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>   mean_percent species                     
#>          <dbl> <chr>                       
#> 1        11.6  Segatella_copri             
#> 2         3.64 Ruminococcus_bromii         
#> 3         3.27 Faecalibacterium_prausnitzii
#> 4         1.95 Agathobacter_rectalis       
#> 5         1.63 Phocaeicola_vulgatus
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

Before computing across tables:

  1. Abundances from different methods are not on the same scale. MetaPhlAn relative_abundance is a percent; Bracken fraction_total_reads is a 0–1 fraction.
  2. Pick one data_type, either full_data (all reads) or rarefied_data (a 1M-read subsample). Most analyses want full_data.
  3. Pick one MetaPhlAn pass. In HUMAnN datasets the bundle’s own MetaPhlAn pass (humann_bundle set) sits next to the main pass (humann_bundle IS NULL).

Each release’s README.md and tables/<table>/schema.json document every column.

HUMAnN gene families

HUMAnN datasets (cmgd_humann3.9-2.3.0, cmgd_humann4a1-2.3.0) also publish per-sample HUMAnN gene-family tables. These are too large for the release tables, so each is its own download from https://cmgd-raw.cancerdatasci.org, listed in the release’s gene-family index. cmgd_genefamilies() takes a release and returns one row per study with gene families; with study, one row per file with its url, size, sha256 and row count, which cmgd_download() fetches and verifies. No HUMAnN dataset is on the public site yet, so this code is shown but not run.

gf_rel <- cmgd_release("cmgd_humann3.9-2.3.0")
cmgd_genefamilies(gf_rel)
gf <- cmgd_genefamilies(gf_rel, study = "ZellerG_2014")
path <- cmgd_download(gf_rel, gf$url[1])
genefamilies <- read.delim(path, check.names = FALSE)
